annotation.evidence_span: Before creating a stream, all streams of the same type with lower-numbered stream IDs MUST be created.
annotation.interpretation_a: This means that before a new stream with ID 'n' is created, all streams of the same type with IDs 1 through n-1 must exist as created objects, even if they are not fully established or active.
annotation.interpretation_b: This means that before a new stream with ID 'n' is created, all streams of the same type with IDs 1 through n-1 must have had a 'create' operation initiated, but not necessarily fully completed.
annotation.justification: The clause states that lower-numbered streams 'MUST be created' before creating a new stream. However, it doesn't specify what 'created' means. Does it require full establishment, or just the initiation of the creation process? This lack of precision leads to two reasonable interpretations with different implementation behaviours.
annotation.missing_information: The definition of 'created' is not precise. Does 'created' mean the stream object exists, or that the stream establishment handshake is complete?
